Issue: Defeat device software installed in diesel vehicles to cheat EPA emissions tests. VW suspended US TDI sales Sep 2015. Settled civil and criminal claims via multidistrict litigation in California. Total US exposure exceeded $20 billion across consumer, government, and criminal settlements.
Class action by approximately 90,000 UK drivers settled in May 2022 for £193 million without admission of liability. Time-barred claims for non-participating drivers cut off from May 2022.
Primary Source: VW AG Annual Report 2025 / Press Reports

Issue: European Commission issued administrative fine in July 2021 for anticompetitive cooperation among German automakers on SCR emissions systems. UK class actions filed from late 2021 following EC decision. No provisions reported.

Ongoing investor lawsuits in German courts including class actions and criminal proceedings arising from Dieselgate disclosure failures. Contingent liability reported at €3.8 billion as of the 2024 annual report.

Hubei Price Bureau, acting under NDRC guidance, fined FAW-Volkswagen Sales Co. RMB 248.6 million ($40.5 million) for organising Audi dealers to fix vehicle, service, and maintenance prices since 2012. Eight Audi dealers in Hubei fined an additional RMB 29.9 million. First-ever antitrust punishment of a foreign carmaker in China. Audi admitted partial breach.
Primary Source: NDRC; Fortune; China Daily; Orrick Antitrust Watch (Sep 2014)

Entity Involved: Volkswagen AG, Audi AG, Porsche AG
Issue: Chinese competition authority initiated proceedings against VW AG, Audi AG, and Porsche AG following the European Commission's 2021 SCR cartel decision. Authorities issued information requests. No fine imposed yet. Proceedings ongoing.

Korea Fair Trade Commission (KFTC) issued administrative fine decision in April 2023 following analysis of the EU SCR cartel case. Fine of approximately €3 million assessed against Audi AG. Volkswagen AG received no fine. Both Audi AG and Volkswagen AG have appealed to the relevant Korean court. Appeal pending.

Entity Involved: SAIC-Volkswagen Automotive Co., Ltd. / Volkswagen AG
Issue: SAIC-VW operated a plant and test tracks near Urumqi in the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region. Human rights groups documented forced labour risks. VW commissioned an audit via Berlin consultancy Löning, which in turn hired CCP-linked Shenzhen firm Liangma. Leaked audit reviewed by Jamestown Foundation researcher Adrian Zenz found methodology failed international SA8000 standards. All 20 Löning staff publicly distanced themselves from the audit. 50 parliamentarians from 23 countries called on VW to withdraw. VW announced plant sale to state-owned buyer in 2024. Plant and two test tracks sold.
Primary Source: Jamestown Foundation (Zenz, Sep 2024); HRW (May 2024); RFA; China Digital Times

Issue: In January 2024 VW voluntarily disclosed to US CBP that vehicles produced for the US market contained a small electronic subcomponent from a supplier added to the UFLPA Entity List in December 2023. CBP impounded thousands of Audi, Porsche, and Bentley vehicles at US ports. VW committed to replacing the affected component across all vehicles globally. Replacement completed by end of March 2024. US Senate Finance Committee May 2024 report found VW had ongoing business ties to Xinjiang manufacturing and that supply chain auditing methods were insufficient.
Primary Source: US CBP; Senate Finance Committee (May 2024); Foley Hoag; HRW

Issue: CMA issued information requests to VW AG. VW filed for judicial review in July 2022 arguing requests exceeded CMA jurisdiction. Court initially ruled in VW's favour in Feb 2023. CMA appealed; appellate court ruled in CMA's favour in January 2024. VW considering further appeal while examining cooperation options.

European Commission and CMA found that Volkswagen, alongside other European, Japanese, and Korean manufacturers and industry associations including ACEA, agreed to avoid paying recycling companies for end-of-life vehicle disposal services, and agreed not to use recyclability data competitively. Investigation conducted via ACEA Working Group Recycling and related sub-groups. EC imposed fine of approximately €128 million on Volkswagen AG. CMA imposed fine of approximately GBP 15 million on Volkswagen AG and Volkswagen Group UK jointly. Proceedings terminated via settlement.
